approach.method_basis: GenMol generates by remasking rather than by building from scratch. A bidirectional masked diffusion model is trained to fill in deleted spans of a molecular fragment sequence, so at generation time you take an existing molecule, blank out one fragment, and let the model iteratively denoise the gap while every surrounding fragment stays fixed. Because the model sees context on both sides, the replacement it writes has to fit what remains, which keeps the output chemically coherent in a way left-to-right generation does not guarantee.
approach.novelty: This root commits to a fragment representation with explicit attachment labels that are round-trip checked during preparation, so the retained context keeps its exact connection points and the replacement block must satisfy them. It freezes the denoiser entirely and adapts per objective only by changing which observed molecules are selected to supply future contexts, ranked by their accepted scores. All learning is therefore in the choice of what to remask, not in the model that fills the gap.

hypothesis: Freeze a corpus-trained bidirectional masked discrete denoiser over SAFE fragment sequences, then repeatedly select high-ranked task-local observed molecules, replace one fragment with a variable-length mask chunk, iteratively denoise the missing tokens while preserving the surrounding context, and use accepted scores to update which whole molecules supply future contexts.

molecular.headline: The cleanest and most consistent chemistry in the round, anchored on one xanthine-like core
molecular.overall_character: Ring closure and aromatic content both reach 100 percent on two objectives and never fall below 98 percent, and cumulated double bonds are effectively absent throughout. The molecules read as coherent medicinal chemistry with correct attachment: pyrazolines, sulfonyl pyrrolidines, halogenated benzoates. Fragment remasking preserves whatever was already there, which shows as a strong shared core across objectives, a dimethyl pyrimidinedione appearing in the top molecules of three of them. Halogen content is high at 48 to 95 percent, and molecule size stays moderate at forty-three to seventy characters.

method_name: GenMol fragment remasking with a corpus-trained discrete denoiser
method_thesis: Anchor the method in GenMol's fragment-remasking mechanism: a bidirectional masked discrete diffusion model generates replacement fragments while retaining the surrounding molecular context. The anchor is described in [GenMol, Sections 4.1-4.2](https://arxiv.org/html/2501.06158v3). For this benchmark adaptation, train a compact denoiser solely on the permitted unlabeled corpus, then freeze it. Start each objective with a fresh archive of its supplied scored molecules. Select high-ranked observed whole molecules as contexts, replace a randomly chosen fragment with a variable-length mask chunk, iteratively sample the missing SAFE tokens, and decode the resulting complete molecule. Generate further completions until the evaluator-announced batch contains distinct canonical structures. Accepted feedback updates context selection and allows improving completions to become future contexts. This root uses the remasking core with observed whole-molecule contexts; the paper's corpus-derived fragment-vocabulary initialization and fragment-attaching stage are not required. The corpus trains the denoiser and supplies unlabeled length statistics, never a molecule pool for ranking or retrieval. The hypothesis is that contextual fragment replacement preserves useful structure while generating improving alternatives, raising the mean of the five independent final Top-1 scores. Task-local selection can respond immediately to feedback without reward-dependent neural training, but useful conditional generation from the permitted preparation remains an empirical prerequisite.

possible_failure_causes: No mechanism execution failure was detected. Proposal efficiency is limited by 3185 invalid decodes and 3262 duplicate outcomes among 9280 internal attempts; another 1383 valid completions were discarded after the announced batch was full.

Most accepted proposals fail to exceed their generating context: 273/1450 beat it and aggregate mean child-minus-context is -0.06991043617790915. This is observed proposal-selectivity weakness, not a failure to learn, denoise or reuse feedback.

Invalid decodes remain common despite lower reconstruction loss. A mismatch between fixed-length reconstruction training and variable-length remasking is a possible cause of the invalid generations, but this run contains no causal ablation to establish that explanation.

applicability_conditions: Confirmed for the supplied screening seed 0 on the five independent objectives. This root has no Parent, and the evidence establishes neither a Parent advantage nor reliability across additional seeds.

All five objectives begin with a fresh archive of the 10 supplied scored molecules; all 300 final archive molecules per objective remained encodable and eligible. Transfer to unencodable or unsplittable initial contexts is unsupported.

The permitted unlabeled corpus supported 180000 round-trip-checked SAFE sequences and a 1714742-parameter bidirectional denoiser, trained for 45000 steps in 797.8744934989954 seconds of recorded preparation. The 1024 fixed validation sequences also selected the published checkpoint; this diagnostic is not an independent test-set score.

The verified representation uses explicit cross-fragment ring-closure labels and BRICS/fine cuts. Emitted proposals preserve nonempty surrounding substructure and attachment semantics; successful chemistry requires syntax-constrained sampling and local invalid/duplicate rejection.

Variable-length replacement and repeated chemistry-token denoising occurred: 973/1450 emissions changed fragment length and 838/1450 required more than one nonattachment-token update. The remaining 612 emissions completed their single nonattachment token in one update after attachment positioning.

Task-local structural locality sometimes improved each objective, and improving completions were reused. Lower average child scores limit the claim to occasional local improvements and positive within-run incumbent changes.

The neural checkpoint remains fixed while accepted whole-molecule scores update context-selection ranks. The observed root uses no corpus molecule/fragment retrieval, autoregressive rollout, graph-edit proposal fallback, objective surrogate, reward-dependent neural training or posterior-sampling selection.

finding_summary.headline: Second highest at 0.495, and the most consistent root across all five objectives
finding_summary.insights: Consistency, not peak performance, is what this node contributes. Its sitagliptin_mpo score of 0.344 is the best in the round and its drd2_docking of 0.908 is third, which no other method combines. The negative context-beating delta is the interesting result: the search improves by keeping the rare good completion and discarding the rest, rather than by proposing better molecules on average. That means throughput of attempts matters more here than proposal quality, which is a different tuning direction from every other lineage. One seed, and the fragment vocabulary itself has not been varied.
finding_summary.results: The macro mean of 0.495 is second of thirteen. It is the only root above 0.20 on every single objective: 0.908 on drd2_docking, 0.591 on deco_hop, 0.424 on zaleplon_mpo, 0.344 on sitagliptin_mpo and 0.207 on median_2. Context selection enrichment was positive on every objective and held under a tie-midrank sensitivity check. Every remasking attempt decoded with an unchanged prefix and suffix, a nonempty retained subgraph, exactly one replacement block and fixed outside attachment labels. One registered measurement came back against expectation: the mean score of a completion minus its generating context is negative in aggregate and on every task, so individual completions usually score worse than the molecule they came from.

finding_summary.headline: Second highest at 0.495, and the most consistent root across all five objectives
finding_summary.insights: Consistency, not peak performance, is what this node contributes. Its sitagliptin_mpo score of 0.344 is the best in the round and its drd2_docking of 0.908 is third, which no other method combines. The negative context-beating delta is the interesting result: the search improves by keeping the rare good completion and discarding the rest, rather than by proposing better molecules on average. That means throughput of attempts matters more here than proposal quality, which is a different tuning direction from every other lineage. One seed, and the fragment vocabulary itself has not been varied.
finding_summary.results: The macro mean of 0.495 is second of thirteen. It is the only root above 0.20 on every single objective: 0.908 on drd2_docking, 0.591 on deco_hop, 0.424 on zaleplon_mpo, 0.344 on sitagliptin_mpo and 0.207 on median_2. Context selection enrichment was positive on every objective and held under a tie-midrank sensitivity check. Every remasking attempt decoded with an unchanged prefix and suffix, a nonempty retained subgraph, exactly one replacement block and fixed outside attachment labels. One registered measurement came back against expectation: the mean score of a completion minus its generating context is negative in aggregate and on every task, so individual completions usually score worse than the molecule they came from.

molecular_assessment.headline: The cleanest and most consistent chemistry in the round, anchored on one xanthine-like core
molecular_assessment.overall_character: Ring closure and aromatic content both reach 100 percent on two objectives and never fall below 98 percent, and cumulated double bonds are effectively absent throughout. The molecules read as coherent medicinal chemistry with correct attachment: pyrazolines, sulfonyl pyrrolidines, halogenated benzoates. Fragment remasking preserves whatever was already there, which shows as a strong shared core across objectives, a dimethyl pyrimidinedione appearing in the top molecules of three of them. Halogen content is high at 48 to 95 percent, and molecule size stays moderate at forty-three to seventy characters.

applicability_conditions: Applies to independent scalar molecular maximization objectives with valid scored initial molecules that can supply encodable fragment contexts; every objective starts with a fresh labeled archive.

The permitted unlabeled corpus must support a compact SAFE denoiser with useful conditional generation within the supplied preparation resources. Published large-scale GenMol results do not establish this prerequisite or transfer to the frozen final Top-1 benchmark.

The SAFE representation and decoder must round-trip relevant chemistry and preserve surrounding context and attachment semantics. The denoiser must generate enough connected, novel fragment completions to maintain the announced batch without an alternative proposal mechanism.

Structural locality must be useful for the current objective: changing a fragment while retaining its context must sometimes yield accepted improvements. Poor improvement rates can coexist with correctly executed denoising.

The root uses observed whole-molecule context selection, frozen unlabeled neural weights, and direct evaluation of fresh completions. Corpus-derived fragment-vocabulary search, fragment attaching, reward-dependent neural training, a learned objective surrogate, and posterior-sampling selection are outside this root.

approach.method_basis: GenMol generates by remasking rather than by building from scratch. A bidirectional masked diffusion model is trained to fill in deleted spans of a molecular fragment sequence, so at generation time you take an existing molecule, blank out one fragment, and let the model iteratively denoise the gap while every surrounding fragment stays fixed. Because the model sees context on both sides, the replacement it writes has to fit what remains, which keeps the output chemically coherent in a way left-to-right generation does not guarantee.
approach.novelty: This root commits to a fragment representation with explicit attachment labels that are round-trip checked during preparation, so the retained context keeps its exact connection points and the replacement block must satisfy them. It freezes the denoiser entirely and adapts per objective only by changing which observed molecules are selected to supply future contexts, ranked by their accepted scores. All learning is therefore in the choice of what to remask, not in the model that fills the gap.
